Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty, smooth, oriented three-manifold without boundary. Let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, let $K$ be a smooth symmetric covariant two-tensor, and let $e,b$ be smooth vector fields tangent to $\Sigma$. For data induced on an embedded spacelike slice $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$, let $n$ be its future unit normal, let $F$ be the smooth two-form of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], and define spatial covectors $\mathcal E,\mathcal B\in\Omega^1(\Sigma)$ by $\mathcal E(X):=F(X,n)$ and $\mathcal B(X):=-({\star_gF})(X,n)$ for $X\in T\Sigma$. Identify these with vector fields using the positive metric $h$: $e:=\sharp_h\mathcal E$ and $b:=\sharp_h\mathcal B$, so in any coordinates $e^i=h^{ij}\mathcal E_j$ and $b^i=h^{ij}\mathcal B_j$. Equivalently, $\mathcal E$ is the restriction of the observer electric covector $E/c$ and $\mathcal B$ the restriction of the observer magnetic covector $B$ of [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]]. For an abstract data tuple not assumed to come from $F$, $e,b$ are simply the specified tangent vector fields. This fixes the convention without adding a potential or an existence assumption.

For the observer-covector comparison above, the smooth normal along $\Sigma$ has local smooth ambient extensions by [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]; shrinking and normalizing an extension gives an observer congruence to which [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]] applies. The restrictions $\mathcal E,\mathcal B$ depend only on $n|_\Sigma$, so they are independent of the chosen extension.

Write $h^{ij}$ for the inverse matrix to $h_{ij}$ and use $h$ to raise every spatial index. Let $D$ and $R(h)$ denote the Levi-Civita connection and scalar curvature of $h$, set $\tau:=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2:=h^{ik}h^{j\ell}K_{ij}K_{k\ell}$, and choose the induced spatial orientation so $\operatorname{vol}_g=\theta^0\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h=-n^\flat\wedge\operatorname{vol}_h$ in a positively oriented normal coframe with $\theta^0(n)=1$. Define the spatial cross product by $h(e\times_hb,w)=\operatorname{vol}_h(e,b,w)$ for each tangent vector $w$.

For the fixed parameters $(\kappa,\Lambda,\mu_0)$ of [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]], the tuple $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ is **constrained electrovacuum initial data** when

$$D_ie^i=0,\qquad D_ib^i=0,$$

$$R(h)+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}\bigl(|e|_h^2+|b|_h^2\bigr),$$

$$D^jK_{ji}-D_i\tau=-\frac{\kappa}{\mu_0}(e\times_hb)_i.$$

Here the last display is an equality of covectors. The scalar-curvature form is the Gauss-Codazzi form of the normal projections in [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]; the sign and $K$ convention are those of [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]]. This definition asserts no existence or uniqueness of a spacetime development.

For the periodic high-regularity class, use the dimensionless coordinate $\theta^i$ and length coordinate $X^i=L_0\theta^i$ of [[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]], for a fixed $L_0>0$. The arrays $h_{ij}$ and $K_{ij}$ are the length-coordinate covariant components with $h_{ij}\in H^{s+1}$ and $K_{ij}\in H^s$. The Sobolev components of $e,b$ are $e_A=h(e,\mathsf e_A)$ and $b_A=h(b,\mathsf e_A)$ in the canonical positively oriented $h$-orthonormal frame $\mathsf e_A$ specified there; thus $e_A,b_A\in H^s$. If $\mathsf e_A=E_A^i\partial_{X^i}$, their coordinate components are $e^i=E_A^i e_A$ and $b^i=E_A^i b_A$. The coefficients $E_A^i$ are smooth functions of the positive matrix $h_{ij}$; on the compact range of each such metric, [[lem-gr-smooth-composition-and-commutator-estimates]] puts them in $H^{s+1}$ and [[lem-gr-periodic-sobolev-algebra]] makes the coordinate components $H^s$ as well.

For these representatives define the spatial connection coefficients by $\Gamma(h)^k{}_{ij}=\tfrac12h^{k\ell}(\partial_{X^i}h_{j\ell}+\partial_{X^j}h_{i\ell}-\partial_{X^\ell}h_{ij})$, with $\partial_{X^i}=L_0^{-1}\partial_{\theta^i}$. On coordinate vector components put $D_i e^j=\partial_{X^i}e^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}e^k$ and $D_i b^j=\partial_{X^i}b^j+\Gamma(h)^j{}_{ik}b^k$; on the covariant tensor $K$ put $D_iK_{jk}=\partial_{X^i}K_{jk}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ij}K_{\ell k}-\Gamma(h)^\ell{}_{ik}K_{j\ell}$. Define $R(h)$ by $R^a{}_{bij}=\partial_{X^i}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jb}-\partial_{X^j}\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ib}+\Gamma(h)^a{}_{ic}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{jb}-\Gamma(h)^a{}_{jc}\Gamma(h)^c{}_{ib}$, followed by the Ricci and scalar contractions of [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]. Sobolev embedding gives $h\in C^{s-1}$ and $K,e,b\in C^{s-2}$; the uniform positive lower eigenvalue makes $h^{-1}$ well defined, and the smooth-composition and algebra suppliers give $\Gamma(h)\in H^s$, $R(h)\in H^{s-1}$, and $D K,D e,D b\in H^{s-1}$. Since $s\ge5$, these constraint terms have continuous representatives, and their displayed equalities mean pointwise equality of those representatives. In the SI interpretation, $K$ and $D$ carry one inverse-length factor, $R(h)$ and $\Lambda$ carry inverse-length squared, and the orthonormal components $e_A,b_A$ have units tesla; the factors $\kappa/\mu_0$ give matching units in the constraints. No numerical parameter values are assigned here.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable, oriented and time-oriented four-manifold with smooth Lorentz metric of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Use its metric-selected connection and curvature convention. Fix $c>0$, $G_N>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and put

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}>0.$$

Within this formulation, $c$, $G_N$, $\mu_0$, and $\Lambda$ are primitive model parameters: respectively, the time-to-length conversion parameter, the gravitational coupling parameter, the electromagnetic normalization parameter identified with vacuum permeability in the SI convention, and the coefficient of the cosmological term. Their values are not derived by this definition, and no numerical value or empirical exactness claim is made here. The coupling $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ is derived from $G_N$ and $c$. For the SI interpretation, $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $G_N$ has units $\mathrm{m^3\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, $\mu_0$ has units $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$, $\kappa$ has units $\mathrm{s^2\,kg^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$, and $\Lambda$ has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. In a length-coordinate chart $x^0=ct$, metric components are dimensionless and curvature components have units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$.

For a smooth real two-form $F\in\Omega^2(M)$, define

$$Q_{ab}(g,F):=F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd},\qquad T^{\rm EM}_{ab}:=\mu_0^{-1}Q_{ab}(g,F).$$

Indices are raised with $g^{-1}$; $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge star of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. The electromagnetic stress tensor $T^{\rm EM}$ is a symmetric covariant two-tensor; in an orthonormal frame its components have energy-density units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. If $n$ is a future unit normal and $(\mathfrak e_1,\mathfrak e_2,\mathfrak e_3)$ is a positively oriented orthonormal spatial triad, define $e_i:=F(\mathfrak e_i,n)$ and $b_i:=\tfrac12\epsilon_i{}^{jk}F(\mathfrak e_j,\mathfrak e_k)$. By [[lem-emg-observer-field-decomposition]], these are $E_i/c$ and $B_i$ in the SI observer convention; both have units tesla.

For sign clarity only, a sourced extension would write $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0J^b$ for a smooth current vector $J$; the source-free system below is the case $J=0$.

The **source-free electrovacuum tensor Cauchy system** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is the system for a smooth Lorentz metric $g$ and smooth real two-form $F$ on $U$ given by

$$G_{ab}[g]+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T^{\rm EM}_{ab}[g,F],\qquad dF=0,\qquad d(\star_gF)=0.$$

Here $G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Sg_{ab}$ is the Einstein tensor. A **spacelike initial hypersurface** is a smooth spacelike embedded three-manifold $i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow U$ with induced Riemannian metric $h=i^*g$ and future unit normal $n$, using [[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]. Its second fundamental form is $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ for tangent vectors $X,Y$. The notation $K=\tfrac12\mathcal L_nh$ requires an induced-metric family: locally near each $p\in\Sigma$, define $\Phi(t,q)=\gamma_{q,n_q}(t)$ by the ambient geodesic with initial position $q$ and initial tangent $n_q$. Smooth dependence of geodesics and the inverse function theorem give, after shrinking around $(0,p)$, a local diffeomorphism $\Phi:(-\epsilon,\epsilon)\times V\to U_p$; its slices remain spacelike after a further shrinking. Put $h_t:=\Phi_t^*g$ on $V$. In local slice coordinates $y^i$, differentiating $(h_t)_{ij}=g_{ab}(\Phi(t,y))\partial_i\Phi^a\partial_j\Phi^b$ at $t=0$ gives
$$\left.\partial_t(h_t)_{ij}\right|_{0}=n^c\partial_cg_{ab}\,\partial_i\Phi^a\partial_j\Phi^b+g_{cb}(\partial_i n^c)\partial_j\Phi^b+g_{ac}\partial_i\Phi^a(\partial_jn^c)=g(\nabla_{\partial_i}n,\partial_j\Phi)+g(\nabla_{\partial_j}n,\partial_i\Phi)=2K_{ij},$$
using metric compatibility, torsion-freeness and symmetry of $K$. Thus $\mathcal L_nh$ denotes only this initial derivative of the local induced-metric family; no global normal foliation or uniform time width is assumed. A hypersurface is a **Cauchy hypersurface in $U$** exactly when every inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to U$ meets it at exactly one parameter value, that is, $\gamma^{-1}[i(\Sigma)]$ has exactly one element, using the causal-curve convention of [[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]. The local initial-data constructions require a spacelike initial hypersurface; they do not assume this global intersection property. The initial data are the induced $(h,K,e,b)$, where $e,b$ are the spatial fields just defined. No global electromagnetic potential is part of this definition.

In the SI convention the electromagnetic two-form has orthonormal-frame components in tesla, $T^{\rm EM}_{ab}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$, and every term of the Einstein equation has units $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. The equations define a mathematical model; they do not assert that the model describes nature or that arbitrary Cauchy data have a development.

Its smooth real $k$-forms are sections of $\bigwedge^kT^*M$, written $\Omega^k(M)$, and $d$ is the exterior derivative of [[lem-emg-lorentz-hodge-calculus]]. A smooth two-form $F$ is **closed** when $dF=0$ and **exact** when $F=dA$ for some smooth real one-form $A$ on the whole base.

By [[def-de-rham-cohomology]], $H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)=Z^2(M)/B^2(M)$, where $Z^2(M)$ is the vector space of closed smooth two-forms and $B^2(M)$ is the vector space of exact smooth two-forms. Thus, for closed $F$, the statement $[F]=0$ means exactly that $F=dA$ for a global smooth one-form $A$. This equivalence is the quotient definition; it does not assert that every closed form is exact.

Identify $\mathbb C$ with $\mathbb R^2$ by $z=x+iy$ and set $U(1)=S^1:=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$. Its topology is the subspace topology. Specify its smooth structure by the four charts

$$V_{x,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon x>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto y,\quad y\mapsto(\epsilon\sqrt{1-y^2},y),$$

and

$$V_{y,\epsilon}=\{(x,y)\in S^1:\epsilon y>0\},\quad (x,y)\mapsto x,\quad x\mapsto(x,\epsilon\sqrt{1-x^2}),$$

for $\epsilon\in\{-1,1\}$, with each coordinate range $(-1,1)$. They cover $S^1$; their transition maps are restrictions of the positive square-root branch and coordinate projections, hence are smooth by [[lem-emg-positive-square-root-smoothness]] and [[thm-ck-euclidean-maps-closed-under-algebra-and-composition]]. In these coordinates multiplication is the restriction of $(x,y)(u,v)=(xu-yv,xv+yu)$ and inversion is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,-y)$, so both are smooth; they are also continuous for the stated topology. Thus this is a smooth Lie group and, in particular, a topological group as required by [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]].

Let $E:\mathbb R\to U(1)$ be $E(t)=e^{it}=(\cos t,\sin t)$; the Cartesian formula is [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. The trigonometric derivative identities of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], iterated, show that $E$ is smooth in the $C^\infty$ sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]: every derivative of either coordinate is $\pm\sin$ or $\pm\cos$, and these functions are continuous by [[cor-differentiable-implies-continuous]]. Surjectivity is [[thm-sine-and-cosine-parametrize-the-unit-circle]]. If $E(t)\in V_{x,\epsilon}$, the chart coordinate $\sin t$ has derivative $\cos t=x\ne0$; if $E(t)\in V_{y,\epsilon}$, the coordinate $\cos t$ has derivative $-\sin t=-y\ne0$. The smooth inverse-function theorem [[lem-choice-free-smooth-inverse-function-theorem-in-euclidean-space]] therefore makes $E$ a diffeomorphism from some open interval about $t$ onto an open circle arc. Every smooth map from an open subset of $M$ to $U(1)$ consequently has, near each point, a smooth real phase lift obtained by composing with such a local inverse.

A **normalized circle-connection datum** on $M$ consists of a supplied countable open cover $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth real one-forms $a_i\in\Omega^1(U_i)$, and a fixed constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require $g_{ii}=1$ and $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on every triple intersection. Around each point of $U_i\cap U_j$, take any smooth real phase lift $f_{ij}$ with $g_{ij}=e^{if_{ij}}$; require

$$
a_j=a_i+df_{ij}
$$

on every such phase-lift neighborhood. If $f$ and $\widetilde f$ are two lifts on a connected neighborhood, [[thm-kernel-and-fibres-of-complex-exponential]] gives $f-\widetilde f\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ pointwise; continuity makes this difference constant, so $df=d\widetilde f$. Thus the compatibility condition is independent of the chosen lift. The globally defined form $\lambda(g):=-i\,g^{-1}dg$ is real, and [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]] together with [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] gives $\lambda(g)=df$ on every phase-lift neighborhood. Hence the equivalent lift-free condition is $a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$.

The right principal $U(1)$-bundle convention is as defined in [[def-principal-g-bundle-and-associated-fiber-bundle]]: it has a continuous right action and locally trivial equivariant product charts, with free and transitive action on each fibre. The compatible transition functions are the gluing data for such a bundle, in the convention that a point with fibre coordinate $z_i$ in chart $i$ has coordinate $z_j=g_{ij}^{-1}z_i$ in chart $j$. No global real-valued angle on $U(1)$ is assumed.

The constant $\kappa_0$ is a chosen normalization with units of webers; it is not Planck's constant and is not a unit of electric charge. On a chart whose coordinates have length units, the normalized connection components $a_i$ have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$; the corresponding local potential $A_i:=\kappa_0a_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-1}$, and its curvature $F_i:=dA_i=\kappa_0\,da_i$ has components $\mathrm{Wb}\,\mathrm m^{-2}$. This definition imposes no flux or charge quantization.

$$Q_{ab}(\mathcal F):=\mathcal F_{ac}\mathcal F_b{}^c-\frac14 g_{ab}\mathcal F_{cd}\mathcal F^{cd},$$

$$d\mathcal F=0,\qquad d(\star_g\mathcal F)=0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}=2Q_{ab}(\mathcal F)$$
at every point of $M$. Here $\star_g$ is the Lorentzian Hodge map determined by $g$ and $o$; on two-forms $\star_g^2=-1$. No material current, matter tensor, global potential, asymptotic flatness, positive mass, horizon, or extension condition is part of this definition.

For flux integration, an **oriented embedded smooth sphere** means a compact smooth two-dimensional manifold $S$ without boundary, homeomorphic to the unit sphere $\{x\in\mathbb R^3:x\cdot x=1\}$, with a specified orientation in the sense of [[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]] and a smooth inclusion $i:S\hookrightarrow M$. Here smooth embedding means an injective immersion that is a homeomorphism onto its image with the subspace topology ([[def-smooth-embedding]]); identify $S$ with that image. The sphere orientation is specified independently of the spacetime orientation; for coordinate spheres used below it is the stated outward orientation.

For a smooth two-form $\eta$ on a neighborhood of $i(S)$, use the pullback convention of [[def-pullback-of-a-differential-form]],
$$(i^*\eta)_p(v,w)=\eta_{i(p)}(di_pv,di_pw),\qquad p\in S,\quad v,w\in T_pS.$$
By [[prop-pullback-of-forms-is-smooth-functorial-and-preserves-wedges]], this is a smooth top form on $S$. Its support is the closure in $S$ of its nonzero locus ([[def-compactly-supported-differential-form]]), hence is closed in compact $S$ and compact by [[thm-closed-subspace-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]. Thus $i^*\eta\in\Omega_c^2(S)$.

Write $\mathcal I_S$ for [[def-integral-of-a-compactly-supported-top-form-on-an-oriented-manifold]]: for a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_j)$ and connected charts $\phi_j$, it sets $\mathcal I_S(\omega)=\sum_j I_{\phi_j}(\rho_j\omega)$, where $I_{\phi_j}$ is the signed chart integral of the compactly supported coefficient. Only finitely many terms are nonzero. The value is independent of charts, partition and refinement by [[thm-global-form-integration-is-independent-of-the-atlas-partition-and-refinement]]. Define the surface notation by
$$\int_S\eta:=\mathcal I_S(i^*\eta).$$
This agrees with [[prop-integration-over-an-oriented-embedded-submanifold]]; a reparametrization here means an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $F:T\to S$ of oriented smooth two-manifolds (a smooth bijection with smooth inverse and orientation-preserving differential). For such $F$, the same value is $\mathcal I_T((iF)^*\eta)$.
The integration definition and its independence theorem assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, already retained in the geometric background below. For $\eta=\mathcal F$ and $\eta=\star_g\mathcal F$, smoothness of the given field and Hodge map makes both pulled-back top forms admissible; their integrals are finite real numbers. Define the geometric electric and magnetic flux parameters by
$$q_e(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\star_g\mathcal F,\qquad q_m(S):=\frac1{4\pi}\int_S\mathcal F.$$
When $M$ and the coordinates have length units, these parameters have units of length. A magnetic flux need not have a global potential; no flux quantization is included. The background Lorentzian geometry and Hodge conventions carry the countable-choice assumption $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of their named suppliers; the algebraic identities in this definition require no additional choice principle.

The inclusion of $S^2$ into $\mathbb R^3$ is smooth with injective differential

$$ (\omega_{S^2})_p(u,v):=\det(p,u,v). $$

$dx^0\wedge dr\wedge\omega_{S^2}$.
